per_unit_rules.note: A row whose source column says 'raw' holds an FM raw_material_supplier cost_system, per kg (the Prisma model documents systemCost as $/kg). Today it decides nothing: etlSupplierProducts copies do not set source (the source note above) and the live profile of public.app_supplier_product (3,000-row sample) has source 100% null, so every row stays price_denominator_unknown (undecided no_rule_holds) until a writer sets source. link_types.description: Customer cards of one party. erp_code (Sage IDCUST) is written by the Sage ETL and is the BC No., but is not unique on app_customer, so it yields candidates. FM<->gold is by the FM code the ETL copies into app_customer.code (TRIM, a stored key compared as text_id), at most stored_by_text_join because the same ETL claims a Portal-native row by that code; the fm-cust-{id} external_id link needs the prefixed-id compare (OPEN-DECISIONS).

link_types.name: same_record_as
link_types.description: Supplier cards of one party. The Portal writes the BC vendor No. from app_supplier.code only for Sage-style codes; pure-digit FM codes are never BC numbers (serializers.ts:150-160, 204-214 @b46934a), so the code pair is a lead until an identifier kind restricts it (OPEN-DECISIONS supplier-code-bc-vendor). FM<->gold: app_supplier.external_id fm-supp-{id} is the ETL's stored key for FM supplier {id} (etlSuppliers; parseFmSupplierId), compared under the fm_supplier_id kind that maps the prefixed and the bare id to one key, so it is verified; a malformed or other-prefix external id joins nothing. The name pair stays a lead for suppliers without that key.

evidence.note: parseFmSupplierId reads app_supplier.externalId fm-supp-{n} or a bare number as FM supplier id n; supplierIdsMatch compares suppliers by that id.

upstream-code.issagestylevendorcode.seri.note: The Portal sends app_supplier.code as the BC Vendor No. only when it is Sage-style (has a letter, not pure digits); pure-digit FM codes are omitted and BC auto-numbers the vendor. workbench.bc_same_company_scope.note: Both ends are BC captures: compare only within one BC company (bc_<book> equal on both ends). BC numbers are unique per company only; masters synced to several books and consolidation copies reuse them (SO vs DSO series: outbox-drain.ts:880-890 @b46934a). Machine-readable today as ontology.schema.link_company_scope / CompiledSchema.company_scope.

upstream-code.silvercustomers.code.note: silver.customers.code = NULLIF(TRIM(public.customer.code), ''); etlCustomers (portal/scripts/etl-silver-to-gold.ts:128-210) writes it to app_customer.code via safeStr (trim) and claims a Portal-native row WHERE code = $1. app_customer.code is a stored copy of the FM code (Customer.code @unique, portal/prisma/schema.prisma:1302), so the pair compares text_id; an FM code with surrounding spaces does not link (missed, never false). Unchanged at c3ffda3.

portal.bc_item_card_price_per_base_uom.note: The Portal writes a BC item card with baseUnitOfMeasureCode = bcUomCode(product uom) and unitCost/unitPrice from that product's per-uom costs: item card prices are per the item's base unit of measure.

portal.fm_raw_costs_per_kg.note: Verified by the Portal against staging data (UAT #136): in raw_material_supplier both costsystem (CAD) and costentry (supplier currency) are per kilogram, not per purchase unit; per-UoM cost = per-kg cost x kgperuofm_c.

portal.fm_pack_costs_per_uofm.note: Packaging reorder: the line uom is packaging_supplier.uofm and its unit cost is costentry, else costsystem_c, used as is (no conversion): packaging costs are per uofm.

portal.supplier_product_system_cost_mixe.note: etlSupplierProducts copies FM raw (per kg) and packaging (per uofm) cost_system into one app_supplier_product.system_cost column, which the Prisma model documents as $/kg (schema.prisma:1615@b46934a).

wb.identity_scoring.note: Weighted identity candidates (Fellegi-Sunter: blocking, field comparison levels, m/u from verified and reviewed pairs) offered for a person's review; a link exists only once plx.review records the decision, projected by ontology/reviews.py link_step as reviewed.
